Joint arthritis.ja1: Osteoarthritis involves progressive cartilage degeneration, altered subchondral bone remodeling, low-grade synovial inflammation, and resultant pain, stiffness, and functional decline.
Joint arthritis.ja2: A structured comparison should address inflammatory pattern, duration of stiffness, symmetry, systemic signs, and objective exam findings.
Joint arthritis.ja3: First-line care prioritizes education, activity modification, weight optimization, exercise therapy, and rational pharmacologic support.
Joint arthritis.ja4: Imaging supports diagnosis when clinical uncertainty or red flags are present; x-ray findings should be interpreted alongside symptoms.

Joint replacement.jr1: Indications include severe pain, marked functional impairment, radiographic degeneration, and failure of conservative treatment.
Joint replacement.jr2: Complications include infection, thromboembolism, dislocation, and implant loosening; early recognition improves outcomes.
Joint replacement.jr3: Counselling should cover realistic expectations, risks, recovery timelines, rehabilitation, and shared decision-making.
Joint replacement.jr4: Rehabilitation is phased with pain control, early mobilization, physiotherapy milestones, and regular functional review.

Sports medicine.sm1: Assessment combines injury mechanism, immediate symptoms, focused exam, and selective imaging for decision support.
Sports medicine.sm2: Tendinopathy often reflects load-related overuse while strains involve acute contractile injury; both require graded rehab.
Sports medicine.sm3: Return-to-play decisions integrate strength, functional tests, confidence, and risk-informed progression.
Sports medicine.sm4: Effective prevention includes structured warm-up, load management, sleep, nutrition, and neuromuscular conditioning.

Spine problems.sp1: Mechanical pain is often positional and non-progressive; red flags suggest urgent pathology and warrant escalation.
Spine problems.sp2: Lumbar radiculopathy management starts conservatively with analgesia, function-focused advice, and selective referral.
Spine problems.sp3: Chronic back pain care emphasizes activity, self-efficacy, multidisciplinary support, and realistic functional goals.
Spine problems.sp4: Surgical referral is considered for severe neurological deficits, cauda equina signs, or refractory disabling symptoms.
